# Hotel industry moves further from labor crisis, but major challenges remain

Immigration policy, a dwindling talent pipeline present long-term hurdles

Hotel staffing issues have been incrementally improving, but challenges such as wage inflation and diminished quality of talent have persisted. (Getty Images)

CoStar News

January 6, 2025 | 2:36 P.M.

Hotel operators believe the hotel industry is continuing to see an easing of the labor crisis that defined the early stages of the post-pandemic recovery, but there are still serious, long-term challenges to getting the best talent.

Sources noted staffing up in major markets with high population density is less difficult than seasonal or remote resorts — which continue to face pressures from both the availability and cost of labor.

"Our destination, leisure resort markets have always been a challenge," said Paul Eckert, executive vice president of operations for Davidson Hospitality Group.

He said his company has had to get creative to address those issues, looking at international student programs for seasonal workers and providing housing.

"We lean on work-and-travel programs in certain markets, and we've tried to come up with game plans by market and what segments work the best," he said, adding that 2025 is still going to be a "relatively challenging year" for labor overall.

Matt Arrants, principal at hotel asset management firm the Arrants Company, agreed with that assessment, noting staffing challenges are acute at the seasonal resorts he oversees across New England. He said those types of properties have to invest in seasonal housing and rely on programs such as H-2B and J-1 visas to thrive.

"One of my properties has invested heavily in seasonal housing, and that's been critical," he said. "It's helped a lot."

One thing hoteliers continue to see as the available pool of talent improves — at least marginally compared to the year prior — is those improvements are coming via quantity of applicants more than the quality of applicants.

"We're getting more applicant flow than we've received in the past, and it continues to get better in certain markets, while some markets still have a lack of depth in terms of overall employable people," said Chris Mellone, vice president of operations for Rochester, New York-based Essex Hotel Management. "It's seemingly rebounded to similar levels to before COVID in terms of just the overall applicant pool, but now I'll say that there's probably less qualified applicants than we were seeing then."

Empowering Growth: Hotel Equities’ learning and development programs 

### Empowering Growth: Hotel Equities’ learning and development programs 

 June 27, 2024 Adam Perkowsky 

Hotel owner, operator and developer Hotel Equities (HE) is guided by 12 value statements. One of them—“hire an attitude and teach them the business”—has led to the company launching several learning and development programs. These initiatives target HE associates who wish to gain valuable knowledge to help them climb the corporate ladder within the company, as well as high school and college students interested in hospitality industry careers.

“We want our leaders to accept responsibility for developing our next talent pool of leaders, and our programs support them in their efforts,” said Nancy Curtin Morris, SVP, talent, HE. “All our training is experiential. We don’t ‘watch,’ we ‘do.’ In our development programs, we show and teach. Then we expect the learner to demonstrate their skills, to practice them and to hone them to become effective leaders. Through practice and repetition—and the opportunity to stumble and maybe even fail—we grow better leaders.”

For talent development within the company, HE runs programs for a variety of levels in the organization. Morris offered insights on what each program has to offer.

The Individual Development Program (IDP) “was created for people just starting in the business who learn general operational and leadership skills, to determine if the hospitality industry interests them to pursue.”

The Management Development Program (MDP) “is the next step on someone’s career journey, and is focused on developing their supervisory, management and leadership skills—with the end goal of stepping into a first or second management level role.”

The Leadership Development Program (LDP) “was specifically designed for leaders in multi-unit roles. This is often overlooked as a huge step in someone’s career—coming out of a single-unit role and understanding the leadership skills needed for multi-unit leadership.”

In 2023, the company also launched a program called HERO (Hotel Equities Road to Onboarding), which offered training for newly onboarded GMs, both at the home unit and in a setting with a group of peer GMs.

Next up, Morris said, “is the relaunch of our director of sales onboarding,” which we’ll begin next month.

Success stories coming out of these programs are plentiful. Some of them even helped the company with its bottom line.

“Each MDP grad must design and execute a project during the program, and they must present their project to the senior leaders in Atlanta, including all C-suite members,” said Morris. “We’ve had projects that increased sales, saved overtime hours and replaced all lightbulbs in the hotel with LED bulbs. We’ve had projects on opening a new venue (beachfront cabanas for rent), taking outsourced services in-house (reducing contract labor) and revamping and renting hotel meeting space that was otherwise comped.”

Hotel Management Training | Hotel Equities

# Talent Development

We offer more than just a job—we provide a path to grow. Enjoy access to our world-class management development programs designed to accelerate your career journey.

# Manager in Training Program

We believe the next generation of hospitality leaders deserves a strong foundation—built on hands-on experience, mentorship, and real opportunity. Hotel Equities’ Manager in Training Program is a 6–9-month program designed for recent college graduates eager to launch a meaningful career in hotel leadership. Participants rotate through most hotel departments, receive personalized coaching, and gain project management experience. It’s ideal for early-career hotel professionals ready to grow and lead.

## Individual Development Program (IDP)

The Individual Development Program (IDP) is a self-paced program focused on building management and technical skills. Guided by their General Manager and/or other property leaders, participants explore 30+ modules from sales to revenue management to gain practical experience and to understand hotel operations through a management lens. The experiential format encourages personal ownership of development, allowing team members to learn at their own pace. IDP supports growth at management and supervisory levels and promotes confidence in daily leadership responsibilities.

## Management Development Program (MDP)

The path to great leadership begins with intentional growth. Our 6-month Management Development Program is built for on-property leads, supervisors, and managers ready to sharpen their leadership and management skills. Participants engage in webinars, cohort learning, one-on-one coaching, and complete a capstone project presented to senior leadership. This experience challenges them to think strategically and lead with confidence—empowering associates to push boundaries, set bold goals, and grow both personally and professionally within Hotel Equities.

## Leadership Development Program

Step into a leadership journey designed just for those with multi-unit responsibilities! Our six-month leadership experience blends flexible, self-paced learning with dynamic classroom sessions and enterprise-wide team projects to challenge multi-unit leaders to think and lead differently.

Through interactive modules and real-world challenges, you'll sharpen the skills needed to lead with confidence at Hotel Equities.

## General Manager Onboarding

The GM Onboarding Experience is a structured journey designed to equip leaders new to Hotel Equities with the tools, training, and support needed to lead with confidence. From The HERO Program (see below) to hands-on resources and coaching, the experience blends culture, operational systems, and leadership development experiences. With clear milestones and consistent guidance, GMs build a strong foundation and continue growing well beyond their first few months—empowered to drive results from day one.

Hotel Equities is offering 6–9-month salaried training programs for college graduates. The length of the program is dependent on your previous experience in the industry-either through internships or job experience.

### MANAGER IN TRAINING

### Program (MIT)

The program consists of placement at a specific hotel, balanced with key opportunities to engage with senior leadership in the company, as well as special assignments (hotel openings, task force).

Management trainees will become part of a collective learning community with other recent college graduates from various universities throughout the country.

Programs Start: Every July

For consideration see contact information on last page.

### EXPECTATIONS

You will be placed at your training hotel for 6-9 months.

During that time, the management trainee is given an opportunity for hands-on experience in all areas of hotel operations, including transitions and new hotel openings.

Upon completion of this program, management trainee are considered for roles such as Operations Managers, Department Head, Sales Manager or Assistant General Manager/Select Service, in any of our hotels throughout the portfolio.

### TASKFORCE / TRANSITION

During your time with Hotel Equities (as a management trainee), you may have the opportunity to participate in hotel openings & transitions.

This is an awesome learning opportunity and a lot of fun!

During these opportunities, you will have a chance to be part of the opening/transition team; working at the new hotel, either with current staff or new hired associates; training them on Hotel Equities culture & processes, as well as brand standards & processes.

This may be a newly built hotel, or a hotel recently acquired by Hotel Equities, for third party management.

Current MIT Class

*As we expand into various countries, possessing a work visa for employment in other countries will be taken into consideration for promotions/transfer opportunities.
